Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

School & learning

student noun

at a university or college

also university student, college student, studies

classical

Quint. 2.10.5: studiōsī, students (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 4.13.11 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. department: medical student: medicīnae studiōsus

studiōsus, studiōsī m.

noun, second declension

a student (of a subject: + genitive)

Classically the adjective, keen on something, and in the plural the learned, students; Pliny the Elder called a book Studiōsus, The Student (Plin. Ep. 3.5.5). A woman student, studiōsa. To be a student, at school or after it, is studēre.

Other words

  • audītor, audītōris m. — a pupil of a teacher, one who attends his lectures

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.54: Dēmētrius Phalēreus Theophrastī audītor (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. student

    To be someone’s student is to hear him: tē, Marce fīlī, annum jam audientem Cratippum (Cic. Off. 1.1).

  • discipulus, discipulī m. — a pupil, a disciple

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.6 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 31, 387

    The pupil of a teacher at any age (see pupil).

  • studēns, studentis m./f. — a student

    noun, third declension, masculine or feminine · also used · modern · Traupman 31, 387

    The present participle of studeō used as a noun; not classical.

  • scholasticus, scholasticī m. — a student or teacher of rhetoric

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.3.5 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. student

    Post-Augustan, of the schools of rhetoric; Vives uses it of any student (Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • huic ego «studēs?» inquam. respondit: «etiam.» «ubi?» «Mediōlānī.»

    “Do you study?” I asked him. “Yes,” he answered. “Where?” “At Milan.”Plin. Ep. 4.13.3

See also pupil, school, teacher, research, subject.
